data.name: Freedom: A Time to Reckon
data.detailed_description:
You assume the character of Carlos Romero, a former soldier who lives in a village situated somewhere in the Zulian region in Venezuela. One day the local guerrilla faction decides to loot and pillage your village, and kill anyone who tries to stand in their way. The protagonist, Carlos, was sleeping when the faction started their raid, but he awoke when he heard the first ringing shots. From the moment he realized what was happening, he knew his life was never going to be the same. Carlos decides to join a group of courageous residents defending their homes and their lives in one of the bloodiest battles their village has ever seen!!

You'll:
  • explore the extent of the destruction and violence
  • fight the guerrilla by using a wide range of various fire weapons
  • hold conversations with civilians and paramilitary defense forces (spoken in Spanish and subtitled in English)
  • save your country from insane disimproval
  • cross fields, seas, canyons, and deserts without getting blown up or shot
  • respawn at checkpoints and continue from there, with unlimited lives
  • get healed automatically after violent fights

Join the empowered, brave rebels and take the fate of the village into your own hands!

reviews.review:
Developed by Displacement Studios and Cazack Games and published by Displacement Studios, Freedom: A Time to Reckon is an independent first-person shooter that builds its identity around a personal tale of courage, resistance, and survival. Instead of placing players in a sprawling global war, the game focuses on a fictional conflict in rural Venezuela, where former soldier Carlos Romero is forced back into combat after guerrilla forces descend upon his peaceful hometown. The narrative frames every encounter through the lens of protecting loved ones and reclaiming a community under siege, giving the campaign a more intimate emotional foundation than many military-themed shooters.

The game's story unfolds across a series of interconnected missions that lead players through villages, rugged landscapes, beaches, deserts, and canyon regions scarred by violence. As Carlos advances, he encounters fellow survivors and local resistance fighters who provide insight into the escalating crisis. Spanish voice acting paired with English subtitles enhances the authenticity of the setting, allowing the world to feel rooted in its cultural backdrop rather than relying on generic military tropes. Although the storytelling remains fairly direct, the focus on civilian resilience and the consequences of conflict gives the campaign a distinctive tone that separates it from more conventional action games.

Combat is built around accessible first-person shooting mechanics that emphasize constant forward momentum. Players make use of a variety of firearms while battling waves of hostile enemies across linear combat zones. Automatic health regeneration removes the need to manage medical supplies, while unlimited respawns at checkpoints encourage experimentation without heavily punishing failure. Exploration occasionally breaks up the action, rewarding players with a closer look at the game's environments and reinforcing the sense of traveling through a country struggling to survive amid armed conflict. The straightforward design makes the experience easy to pick up, even if it lacks the tactical complexity found in more advanced shooters.

Visually, Freedom: A Time to Reckon reflects the realities of its independent development. Character models, environmental detail, and animations are functional rather than cutting-edge, and players expecting modern blockbuster production values will quickly notice the technical limitations. However, the game compensates by committing to its atmosphere and setting. The environments effectively communicate the destruction left behind by the invasion, while the varied locations help prevent the journey from becoming visually repetitive. Despite its modest presentation, there is a genuine effort to immerse players in a believable struggle rather than simply presenting a sequence of disconnected firefights.

What ultimately makes the game memorable is its willingness to explore a story that is rarely represented within the genre. Instead of relying solely on explosive spectacle, it attempts to portray the determination of ordinary people standing against overwhelming odds. While some aspects of the gameplay remain simple and the overall execution occasionally falls short of its ambitions, the sincerity behind its narrative and world-building gives it a unique appeal. Players interested in independent shooters with an emphasis on story and setting may find its perspective refreshing, even if the mechanics themselves remain familiar.

Freedom: A Time to Reckon is not a revolutionary first-person shooter, but it succeeds in delivering a focused campaign that combines accessible gameplay with a heartfelt narrative about defending one's home. Its uncommon setting, grounded premise, and commitment to portraying local resistance provide an experience that stands apart from many generic military titles. Although technical shortcomings and relatively basic combat prevent it from reaching greater heights, the game's ambition and thematic direction make it a worthwhile experience for players seeking a different kind of action adventure.

Rating: 5/10

content_descriptors.notes: This game contains frequent combat violence, including gunfire, killing, blood, and gore. The story includes a guerrilla attack on a village, looting, pillaging, and civilian danger. There is no sexual content. There is a side quest where the main character gets offered drugs (mention only) and refuses it.
